why_trail.why: Rework, not re-implementation: g2's code landed at b8557ff4 and is approved. Four artifacts assert 'removing it removed no guard'; the reviewer measured that false on the leaseless path. Admiral R1 accepts the widening and orders the CLAIM narrowed, not the code. My job is four prose repairs plus B2's one-line test fix, with zero executable change under scripts/.

Mechanism verified at source and it matches the handoff exactly. require_session gates only MUTATING_VERBS and returns early when _active_lease is None; _active_lease treats a RELEASED lease as absent, so never-claimed and released are the same path. MUTATING_VERBS includes start/advance/record/attest/attach — all state writers. The narrowed claim can therefore be made true without any code change.

All three copies now narrow the claim identically: the lease guards wherever a lease exists; on a spine with no active lease (never claimed, or claimed and since released) the engine asserts nothing about location; the mutating verbs write state into a foreign tree; under an active lease nothing changed; a forgeable guard is not the same as no guard; the widening is accepted, not a no-op. docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's next paragraph ('Nothing checks at engine level') now agrees with the one above it instead of contradicting it. The C6 drift check is proven red against b8557ff4.

B2 repaired and measured. Added the self.worktree call as its own test method, matching the class's one-method-per-cwd shape: 13 tests/18 subtests -> 14/27. Measured under the reviewer's stamp-reading mutant, with the mutation asserted applied: from the spine's own worktree the wrong-case row separates (exit 0 vs exit 1); from a foreign cwd all 7 stamp-carrying rows refuse identically, so the case row discriminated nothing there. Mutant turns the file red (12 failed) and names the added test; engine restored byte-identical by sha256; file green again.

Verification sweep. Zero executable change under scripts/ proven by AST comparison with docstrings stripped, demonstrated red against one added executable line. Targeted gate check green. Full suite cache-cleared with CREW_SCRATCH_DIR scrubbed. map/ is NOT byte-identical: C5's added test method takes tests.test_spine_origin_isolation from 31 to 32 entities, so the map was regenerated per the Map Anchors conditional and is asserted settled under a repeat build.

amendments.reason: My original c2 check was one that cannot fail: its clauses were separated by ';' so only 'test ! -e scripts/checklist_engine.py.orig' decided the exit, and that file never existed. Replace it with the measurement harness itself, which asserts the mutation applied, reproduces the own-worktree vs foreign-cwd separation, requires the mutant to go red naming the added test, and verifies the engine is restored byte-identical by sha256. The handoff gives the implementer authority over how the B2 measurement is structured.

Three authoring fixes. c1: the handoff's grep uses base 9ff86f2d, which since the 6a4035d2 merge of main also sweeps up lanes A and E, so it no longer isolates this lane; and its filter strips # comments but not docstring bodies, making it a shape argument. Replaced with an AST comparison against HEAD that strips docstrings and proves executable content is unchanged — demonstrated red against one added executable line. c3: used bash-only PIPESTATUS, which the engine runs under a POSIX shell. c4: was convoluted and could pass wrongly; replaced with an empty git status --porcelain over map/, which catches modified AND untracked output.

The handoff expected map/ byte-identical because it judged this rework changes no entities. C5 — which the handoff itself mandates — adds a test method, so tests.test_spine_origin_isolation goes 31 -> 32 entities and the totals 4822 -> 4823. The Map Anchors rule 'regenerate only if entities change' therefore fires, and tests/test_code_map.py::MapTreeFreshnessTests requires the regeneration or the suite is red. The correct assertion is not 'unchanged' but 'settled': a fresh build is idempotent, so the second build reproduces the first exactly.
